title: mcp-server cannot reach db-api: all BigQuery-backed MCP tools fail
description:
The standalone mcp-server (/mcp path, used by external MCP clients) has NEVER been able to reach db-api, so every BigQuery-backed tool returns 'BigQuery API URL not configured'.

Confirmed failing live on daly (2026-07-21): query_bigquery, get_bigquery_schema, get_asm_qtl_by_gene, get_open_chromatin_by_gene, get_variant_effect_by_gene.

Two independent causes, BOTH must be fixed:
1. BIGQUERY_API_URL is set in k8s/deployments/chat-backend.yaml but has never existed in k8s/deployments/mcp-server.yaml (git log -S confirms no commit ever added it).
2. NetworkPolicy allow-ingress-db-api (k8s/network-policies/policies.yaml:137-151) admits only app=chat-backend; monitor-policy.yaml adds monitor. mcp-server is not permitted, so even with the env var set the call would be blocked.

Manifests are profile-independent => affects finngen AND daly equally.

chat-backend is unaffected (has the env var and is allowed by policy), so the web UI agent's BQ tools work; only the standalone MCP server is impacted.

Note these tools are BigQuery-by-design: results-api has no by-gene open_chromatin endpoint, so executor.py:824 resolves gene->coords via gene_annotations_v.

Decision needed: opening db-api to mcp-server is a network-isolation change, not just a config fix.
notes: Config fix committed cb18545 (BIGQUERY_API_URL on mcp-server.yaml + mcp-server podSelector on allow-ingress-db-api NetworkPolicy). Left OPEN: takes effect only after cluster rollout (scripts/rollout.sh mcp-server + re-apply NetworkPolicy). Close after deploy verifies BigQuery-backed MCP tools work.
close_reason: Verified fixed live on finngen (2026-07-24). After deploy: running mcp-server has BIGQUERY_API_URL set; allow-ingress-db-api NetworkPolicy admits app=mcp-server; from pod mcp-server-75fd7c8644 TCP connect to db-api:8080 succeeds (was TimeoutError), /health=200, and POST /query 'SELECT 1 AS ok' returns 200 rows=[[1]]. title: Phase 0: decide ChromBPNet row-scale thresholding policy
description: Count ChromBPNet variant-score rows (132 contexts x variants, potentially billions). Decide thresholding (significant/non-zero only, or top-N per context) before sizing tabix/BQ. Biggest scale risk. Gates the Marderstein munge task.
design:
RECOMMENDED DEFAULT thresholding policy (empirical cutoff + row counts to be CONFIRMED once data is downloaded — blocked on .1). Keep this task OPEN.
Problem: ChromBPNet = 132 contexts x all variants (~3 billion predictions in the paper). Do NOT store the full cross-product.
Default:
- ChromBPNet -> variant_effect (model=chrombpnet), LONG. Emit a row only for (variant, context) pairs that pass a significance/effect threshold, NOT all 132 contexts per variant. Prefer the per-context significance calls provided by the Synapse release if present; else keep per-context empirical mlog10p >= 3 (p <= 1e-3) OR abs(chrombpnet_logfc) in the top 1 percent per context. Always set is_significant and mlog10p so the cutoff is transparent and re-filterable.
- Retain a variant if significant in ANY context (so by_variant lookups return it); emit its passing contexts, plus optionally its single top context.
- FLARE -> variant_effect (model=flare): keep the FULL released FLARE prioritized-variant set (already curated and far smaller); pan-context rows with cell_type/tissue NULL.
Rationale: bounds storage to variants with a real predicted effect somewhere (millions, not billions) — exactly what the query needs. Empirical step (after .1): count rows at this cutoff, confirm the significance fields the release actually provides, adjust cutoff to a sane table size.
close_reason: Decision made: default thresholding policy adopted (recorded in --design). Empirical row-count confirmation happens inside the Marderstein munge task (.13), which applies and tunes the default; no separate gate needed.

title: test suite has order-dependent failures under pytest-randomly
description:
Found while validating genetics-results-suite-2cl/-qdf. PRE-EXISTING and reproducible on pristine HEAD — confirmed NOT caused by that work (a reviewer built a tree differing only by a test-fixture move and got byte-identical failure sets).

genetics-mcp-server: with pytest-randomly active, TestAdminAuthGuards::test_dev_mode_allows_any_user (expects 200, gets 404) and ::test_non_admin_denied_when_auth_required (expects 403, gets 404) fail under some seeds. Measured: seeds 12345 and 20260804 FAIL; seeds 1, 42, 999, 7 PASS. Roughly a 1-in-3 hit rate. With -p no:randomly the suite is green.

The tests pass when test_admin_router.py runs alone under the failing seed, so the leak comes from OTHER modules running first, and no single module reproduces it in isolation — it needs a combination.

Diagnosed causes (not fixed):
- config/settings.py get_settings() is @lru_cache'd; tests that call it without clearing the cache leave a stale Settings instance behind, and admin_required then sees enable_admin_page=False and 404s.
- auth/dependencies.py:14 evaluates _require_auth = os.environ.get('REQUIRE_AUTH', ...) at IMPORT time, so patching os.environ later does not update it.

Fix likely means an autouse fixture clearing get_settings.cache_clear() between tests, and reading REQUIRE_AUTH through settings rather than at import time.

This matters beyond flakiness: every 'full suite green' claim in this epic's task history was measured on whatever seed happened to run.
close_reason:
Landed in genetics-mcp-server commit adb57ef. Suite 810 passed / 74 deselected on -p no:randomly and on seeds 12345, 20260804, 1, 987654321 — the first two being the known-bad ones.

THE TICKET'S DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG and was corrected during implementation. It blamed a stale @lru_cache on get_settings(); the two failing tests already call cache_clear() themselves. The real cause: test_temperature.py called importlib.reload on the settings module, rebinding config.settings.get_settings to a new function object with its own empty cache while config/__init__.py kept re-exporting the old one. admin_required reads the package handle, the tests cleared the submodule handle. A reviewer proved causality by re-injecting the reload into the fixed tree and reproducing the exact failure set.

The reload was never needed (every Settings field reads os.environ in a default_factory) and was latently harmful (the module calls load_dotenv() at import, so a reload resurrects an env var a test just removed).

SEPARATE FINDING, now fixed: pytest-randomly was neither installed nor declared, so -p no:randomly was a silent no-op and every seed sweep in this epic ran against ad-hoc installs. Declared and pinned exactly (the seed-to-order mapping moves between versions), with shuffling left on by default — an undeclared plugin is how this went unnoticed.

Follow-up filed for the REQUIRE_AUTH two-sources-of-truth test trap.

title: llm_config_db: write accessors leave the transaction open on failure
description:
PRE-EXISTING, found while reviewing genetics-results-suite-s5y.4. In genetics-mcp-server src/genetics_mcp_server/db/llm_config_db.py, none of these write accessors roll back on failure: save_tool_description, add_user_comment, delete_user_comment, save_user_setting, delete_user_setting, create_api_token, revoke_api_token, validate_api_token.

Each is a single DML, so SQLite has already backed out that statement's own changes and no partial data is pending. But the transaction stays OPEN and holds the write lock against every other writer of llm_config.db until that thread happens to commit something else. Connections are thread-local and cached for the process lifetime, so a long-lived server thread can hold the lock indefinitely.

The instruction-set accessors added in s5y.4 have rollback guards and a _discard_stale_transaction helper that incidentally cleans this up whenever one of them next runs on the same thread — nothing else does.

Fix: mirror the try/except BaseException -> rollback; raise pattern from create_instruction_set, and move conn.commit() inside the try.
close_reason:
Landed in genetics-mcp-server commit 56f2341. Suite 770 passed / 74 deselected, stable over 6 repeat runs; 20 of 21 new tests verified to fail against the unfixed source.

DELIBERATE DEVIATION on the auth path, verified security-neutral by two independent reviewers: validate_api_token swallows a failure of its trailing bookkeeping UPDATE (last_used_at + rolling expiry) and returns the user anyway, rather than raising. Revocation (is_active=1 in the SELECT's WHERE) and expiry are both decided BEFORE the try, from committed state, so no invalid/expired/revoked token can authenticate. The deadline is frozen rather than pushed on failure, so a persistently failing write ages a token out rather than keeping it alive. Old behaviour was strictly worse: the raise became a 500, mcp-server read that as 401, and the poisoned connection failed every subsequent validation on the same thread — one transient SQLITE_BUSY became a lasting 401 outage for all API-token users until pod restart.

Scope note: read accessors also got _discard_stale_transaction (12 methods the ticket did not name). Kept as defence-in-depth and documented as such, not as a live bug fix.

Follow-up filed: genetics-results-suite-4um (chat_history_db.py has the identical bug class).

title: Feature: user-authored Instructions for chat
description:
Users can create and store multiple named sets of additional instructions (like Claude Desktop 'profiles', e.g. 'I'm a statistician') and select one per chat use case. The selected profile's text is appended to the LLM system prompt on each chat request.

UI lands beside the existing brief/detailed Answer selector in the chat options row (genetics-results-browser src/features/chat/LLMChat.tsx). Storage is per-user in the DB (genetics-mcp-server SQLite llm_config_db, which already has user_settings_history and an orphaned user_instructions_history table). Backend prompt assembly mirrors the verbosity_prompt() pattern in config/defaults.py + chat_api.py.

Spans repos: genetics-mcp-server (API + DB + prompt), genetics-results-browser (UI + types), genetics-results-suite (docs of record).

Naming to be decided as part of planning.
design:
Alternative 2 selected: first-class entity, server-resolved by id, split cached system block.

Name: UI label 'Instructions', code noun instruction_set. Rejected 'profile' (already means tool_profile in the same options row, the daly/finngen deploy config_profile, and results-api app/config/profiles/), 'persona' (the suite spec uses it for the APP_NAME assistant persona, and the text describes the user not the assistant) and 'context' (the same row renders a 'Conversation context' usage bar).

Key decisions:
- The chat request carries an id only; the server loads the body scoped to the authenticated user, so prompt text is never client-supplied and an answer is always attributable to a stored set.
- System prompt splits into two cached blocks: shared default+verbosity (one global cache entry per verbosity value) and the per-user envelope on the spare 4th breakpoint. ~$0.0025 per incremental write vs ~$0.043 for full-block refragmentation vs ~$0.05 per 25-iteration turn uncached.
- Selection: global-per-user default in user_settings_history, overridden per request, recorded per message on chat_messages. Per-session storage rejected: it needs a session-mutation endpoint and makes 'which wins' unanswerable when the selector moves mid-conversation.
- Archive rather than delete, so historical chat_messages rows stay resolvable.
- Unknown id is ignored, never 422 — same rule as verbosity.
- Folded in from the other alternatives: seeded clonable example sets in the dialog (from Alt 3), and the ORDER BY changed_at DESC, id DESC settings fix (from Alt 1).

Out of scope, documented rather than built: subagents (their reports are intermediate artifacts the main agent rewrites) and the MCP server path (no server-side system prompt, _validate_user_token discards identity, no llm_config.db volume mounted).

Not part of this epic, but decide separately: ChatRequest.system_prompt (chat_api.py:209) lets any authenticated user replace the entire system prompt with no gate — a strictly larger hole than the feature going in beside it.

description:

Implement RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata so MCP clients (Claude connectors, ChatGPT, brainzzz) auto-discover the authorization server:

title: Feature: Direct OAuth (Keycloak) auth for MCP server — GeneGenie / brainzzz
description:
Let external web applications (first: brainzzz) connect to the GeneGenie MCP server via a standard OAuth 2.1 flow, instead of a shared api-token. Add this as a FOURTH bearer-validation path alongside the existing three (MCP_API_KEY shared secret, Google Identity Token JWT, per-user API token) — nothing existing is removed.

WHY: IAP/Google ID-Tokens don't fit a third-party app acting on behalf of its own users (audience-bound, no consent/refresh, users not on our email allow-list). MCP's HTTP transport defines an OAuth 2.1 profile where the MCP server is an OAuth *resource server* and clients auto-discover the *authorization server*. The daly/GeneGenie deployment already runs Keycloak as a full OIDC AS (https://auth.<domain>/realms/genetics, ENABLE_KEYCLOAK on for daly), so Keycloak is the authorization server and a 'web application type' OAuth client registered there is exactly what's needed.

SCOPE: GeneGenie (daly profile) only for now. finngen/FinnGenie has Keycloak OFF (Google-direct) and is out of scope.

DESIGN CONTRACT (shared across subtasks):
- Authorization server = Keycloak realm 'genetics'; issuer https://auth.<domain>/realms/genetics.
- MCP resource canonical URL (RFC 8707 resource indicator / RFC 9728 resource identifier) = https://genegenie.broadinstitute.org/mcp.
- Keycloak issues access tokens (JWT) with aud including that resource URL (via an audience mapper / dedicated client scope on the brainzzz client).
- MCP server validates: signature via Keycloak JWKS, iss match, aud includes resource URL, exp; THEN the existing email/domain allow-list (settings.allowed_emails / allowed_email_domains, already fed by the bearer-auth-allowed ConfigMap).
- Discovery: MCP server serves /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource (RFC 9728) pointing at the Keycloak issuer, and returns WWW-Authenticate: Bearer with resource_metadata=... on 401. The authorization-server metadata itself is served by Keycloak (already on auth.<domain>).

Code work is split between the sibling repo ../genetics-mcp-server (validation + discovery + settings) and this repo genetics-results-suite (deployment env + auth-gateway routing + docs). Plus Keycloak client config (ops).

title: Phase 0: finalize EpiMap 18-state storage + open/active state set
description: Decide how the ChromHMM 18-state label is stored (score_type=chromhmm_18state + state token placement) and which states count as open/active (TSS/enhancer/transcribed). Gates the EpiMap munge task.
design:
EpiMap ChromHMM 18-state modeling for the open_chromatin product.
Model = Roadmap/EpiMap 18-state (observed_aux_18), 833 biosamples, hg38 CALLS.
INCLUDE (accessible/active regulatory subset) as open_chromatin rows:
  active promoter: TssA, TssFlnk, TssFlnkU, TssFlnkD
  active enhancer: EnhA1, EnhA2, EnhG1, EnhG2, EnhWk
  poised/bivalent (accessible, tagged): TssBiv, EnhBiv
EXCLUDE (not open peaks): Tx, TxWk, ZNF_Rpts, Het, ReprPC, ReprPCWk, Quies.
State storage (NO schema change): encode the exact state in score_type as chromhmm:<State> (e.g. score_type=chromhmm:EnhA1); assay=chromHMM; score=NULL (presence-based — ChromHMM is a categorical segmentation, so row existence = state called in that biosample).
Agent-facing regulatory_class grouping (map in the MCP tool description, NOT stored): Tss* -> promoter, Enh* -> enhancer, *Biv -> bivalent.
Labels: cell_type = verbatim EpiMap biosample name; tissue from EpiMap sample metadata (GROUP/Anatomy column); life_stage=adult unless the biosample metadata marks it fetal/embryonic; condition=unknown.
Do NOT import EpiMap DNase layer (that is the Meuleman DHS index, which was dropped).
close_reason: Resolved: EpiMap active/accessible state subset + state-in-score_type encoding decided. Decision recorded in --design.

title: REQUIRE_AUTH has two sources of truth in the chat backend
description:
Found while fixing genetics-results-suite-8r4. PRE-EXISTING, not a production bug, but a live test trap.

genetics-mcp-server reads REQUIRE_AUTH twice:
- src/genetics_mcp_server/auth/dependencies.py:14 snapshots it at IMPORT time into the module global _require_auth, used by auth_required and admin_required.
- src/genetics_mcp_server/chat_api.py:260 re-reads os.environ['REQUIRE_AUTH'] per request.

Safe in production: nothing in src/ writes os.environ at runtime (verified — no assignment, setdefault, putenv or update anywhere), and in k8s the value is fixed for the process lifetime, so the two always agree.

The problem is in tests: patch('...dependencies._require_auth', True) moves one and not the other, while patch.dict(os.environ, {'REQUIRE_AUTH': 'true'}) moves the other and not the one. So /chat/v1/auth's is_admin can disagree with admin_required's gate under test — exactly the class of test-isolation trap 8r4 was about.

Fix: route both through settings rather than reading os.environ in two places.

Also worth knowing: seeds quoted in bug reports are only meaningful while pytest-randomly stays pinned at the version 8r4 set. Bumping it resets that history.

title: admin feedback pagination can duplicate or skip an item on a same-second tie
description:
Found while validating genetics-results-suite-s5y.5. PRE-EXISTING, out of that task's scope.

genetics-mcp-server routers/admin.py:269 merges list_all_user_comments() with session comments, Python-stable-sorts by created_at, then slices items[offset:offset+limit].

created_at is CURRENT_TIMESTAMP with one-second resolution, so two submissions in the same second tie. The input order from the DB is unconstrained (ORDER BY created_at DESC with no id tiebreak), so the page boundary can shift between requests — an admin paging through feedback can see one item twice or miss one entirely.

This is the same root cause as s5y.5 but a different symptom: no single 'current value' is derived, so s5y.5 deliberately left the comment listings alone. The fix is the same shape — add an id tiebreak to the ORDER BY in get_user_comments / list_all_user_comments, and make the merge sort key (created_at, id).
close_reason:
Landed in genetics-mcp-server commit e636200 (shared with 2cl). Verified across all 40,320 permutations of an 8-row input spanning both sources: exactly one merged order, every item appearing exactly once when walking pages with the input reshuffled between requests. HEAD reproduced the reported symptom exactly (one item twice, another never).

A BUG WAS INTRODUCED AND CAUGHT IN REVIEW: the first fix stringified the comment id for tuple homogeneity, which sorts lexicographically — ids 8,9,10,11 rendered as 9,8,11,10, exactly negating the ORDER BY the same fix added. The stringification was also unnecessary: 'source' is compared first, so an int id is never compared against a session uuid. Raw ids now, with the source discriminator proven load-bearing by mutation (dropping it raises TypeError).

Recorded reason corrected: the earlier claim that making the user-comment reads timezone-aware would break this merge key was tested and found FALSE — the key stays total and identically ordered because both stamps render as a fixed 19-char prefix. The decision not to touch them stands on scope grounds only; genetics-results-suite-ni9 owns them.

Also filed from this work: genetics-results-suite-8r4 (pre-existing order-dependent suite failures under pytest-randomly).

title: llm_config_db: singular config reads crash on a NULL or blank changed_at
description:
Found while validating genetics-results-suite-s5y.5. PRE-EXISTING, unchanged by that task.

In genetics-mcp-server src/genetics_mcp_server/db/llm_config_db.py the singular and plural accessors diverge on a malformed timestamp:
- get_user_setting / get_tool_description RAISE TypeError from datetime.fromisoformat(None) when every row for a key has a NULL changed_at, and ValueError from fromisoformat('') on a blank-string stamp.
- get_user_settings / get_tool_descriptions silently drop the key instead.

The columns carry no NOT NULL, so both states are reachable. This contradicts the convention s5y.3 and s5y.4 established in this same file — _as_utc_or_epoch and COALESCE(changed_at, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) — whose own test says 'a read must degrade rather than fail a chat turn'.

Fix: route these accessors through _as_utc_or_epoch, which would also let the 'changed_at IS NOT NULL' clauses in the plural queries go away.

Left alone in s5y.5 under the don't-change-unrelated-code rule, but s5y.5's new comments now document the hazard without resolving it.
close_reason:
Landed in genetics-mcp-server commit e636200 (shared with qdf — the two were implemented together as they touch the same file and are the same defect class). Suite 810 passed / 74 deselected, clean on seeds 1/42/999/7. 15 of 17 mutants killed.

Three review rounds. Round 1 core verified exhaustively (600 randomized differential cases, 13 adversarial scenarios) — no winner-selection semantics changed. Round 2 caught that the round-1 test rewrite silently dropped the ONLY mutation coverage for a dropped changed_at join in get_tool_descriptions. Round 3 caught that a mutant I had accepted as untestable was in fact deterministically pinnable, and that the write-path changes were entirely uncovered (3 surviving mutants).

Two reviewers contradicted each other on whether COALESCE could let a NULL row win. Resolved empirically: coalescing to a sentinel the column never holds IS equivalent to IS; coalescing to one it DOES hold ('', 0, or CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) collapses real rows onto the NULL key. Only CURRENT_TIMESTAMP can beat a genuinely usable stamp.

Scope note: the four reads now return timezone-aware UTC, so the saves and get_tool_description_history were routed the same way to keep the endpoint family consistent. Nothing is STORED differently — both saves rely on DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, and the aware value exists only in the returned object. Verified across the whole suite that no client reads changed_at.

Two CURRENT_TIMESTAMP-sentinel mutants remain alive, documented rather than tested: killing them needs a row stamped inside the query's own second, which would be clock-flaky.

Follow-up filed: genetics-results-suite-ni9 (the sibling comment/history accessors still crash on the same input).

title: chat_history_db: same commit-without-rollback bug class as llm_config_db
description:
Found by the blind validator while validating genetics-results-suite-y5d.

genetics-mcp-server src/genetics_mcp_server/db/chat_history_db.py has the identical shape y5d fixed in llm_config_db.py: write methods execute DML then commit() with no try/except rollback guard. Python's sqlite3 with isolation_level='' auto-opens a transaction before DML, so a failed statement or a failed commit leaves the thread-local cached connection inside an open transaction, holding the write lock against every other writer until that thread happens to commit something else.

chat_history_db DOES set PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL (line ~87), which reduces reader/writer contention and makes the trigger less likely than in llm_config_db — but it does not eliminate writer/writer contention or a failed commit.

Fix: apply the pattern y5d established — _discard_stale_transaction on entry, DML and commit() inside a try, except BaseException -> rollback; raise. Check whether any method there does multiple DMLs under one commit before applying a blanket discard.

Out of scope for y5d, which was explicitly scoped to llm_config_db.

title: llm_config.db does not enable WAL, unlike chat_history.db
description:
PRE-EXISTING, found while reviewing genetics-results-suite-s5y.4. genetics-mcp-server src/genetics_mcp_server/db/llm_config_db.py _create_connection leaves journal_mode=delete with the default 5s busy_timeout.

The sibling db/chat_history_db.py:87 DOES set PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL, with a comment about not blocking live writers — so llm_config_db is the odd one out.

Consequence: 'database is locked' is the most likely failure mode for every writer of this DB, and it became slightly more consequential in s5y.4 because create_instruction_set now takes an exclusive write lock via BEGIN IMMEDIATE. The critical section is sub-millisecond against a 5s timeout, so this is not urgent.

Deliberately NOT changed in s5y.4: switching journal modes affects every table in this database, which is broader than that task's scope and needs a decision on the live PVC file.
close_reason:
Landed in genetics-mcp-server commit 5e31dbd. Suite 773 passed / 74 deselected across 3 random orderings, zero flakiness; all 3 new tests verified to fail without the pragma.

Data safety verified independently by two reviewers: 120 kill -9 trials swept across the conversion window (4 outcome classes, all integrity ok, all rows intact), disk-full, read-only, and two-process races. Fully reversible both ways — the pre-change image reads and writes a converted file fine, and PRAGMA journal_mode = DELETE restores it.

TICKET PREMISE CORRECTED: a reader is NOT blocked by a writer merely holding BEGIN IMMEDIATE (that takes RESERVED, which coexists with readers' SHARED). The exclusion is at COMMIT time. The naive version of the requested test would have passed in both modes and proved nothing; the tests written instead cover both real directions.

Availability trade documented: durability is unchanged (synchronous stays FULL) but a WAL database must write -shm to be read at all, so a read-only or full volume that previously served reads now serves none. chat_history.db already had this property on the same PVC.

Beyond ticket scope, kept deliberately: test fixtures across 5 files now close connections and remove -wal/-shm sidecars. Fixing conftest alone left 196 files stranded per run. The pre-existing litter (~34,672 files, ~385 MB) in /tmp was NOT deleted — that is the user's machine.

title: Fix misleading schedule comment in analyze-conversations-cronjob.yaml
description: The header comment in k8s/deployments/analyze-conversations-cronjob.yaml says the job runs 'after the daily chat-data disk snapshot window', but the CronJob schedule is 02:30 and the terraform chat_data_snapshots disk snapshot runs at 03:00 — so the job runs BEFORE the snapshot (which is actually the desirable ordering: that night's 03:00 snapshot captures the 02:30 analysis). Correct the manifest comment to describe the ordering accurately (analysis 02:30, snapshot 03:00 captures it). Docs (project-spec.md) already describe the timing correctly; only the manifest comment needs fixing. Low priority, cosmetic + ops-accuracy.
